context: Letter-value (boxen) plot comparing five distribution groups (Symmetric, Right-skewed, Left-skewed, Bimodal, Heavy-tailed) with nested boxes encoding quantile depth levels (Fourths through Sixty-fourths), plus a chart/table toggle
first_impression: Immediately readable — the nested-box shapes make distributional differences salient across the five groups without visual clutter.
what_works: The sequential blue palette maps depth cleanly without categorical confusion; the varying silhouette shapes (diamond, pyramid, inverted pyramid, rectangle, tall tower) encode distributional character so effectively that group differences are graspable in one glance. Five shades for five depth levels stays well within color-discrimination limits.
what_doesnt: The Bimodal group's shape does not visually signal bimodality — it reads as a near-uniform or platykurtic box, not two peaks, so the label does extra cognitive work the chart should be doing. The lightest blue swatch (Sixty-fourths) in the legend is barely distinguishable from the background, making that legend entry hard to match back to the chart at a glance.
